stem: Which of the following is the first artificially prepared element ?
expl: The first artificially prepared element is Technetium (Tc), whose atomic number is 43. Its molar mass is 98.91 g mol–¹. It was isolated in 1937 by Carlo Perrier and Emilio Segrè.

stem: in a car battery, electrolyte substance used is-
expl: A secondary cell is used in cars. In a secondary cell, a dilute solution of sulphuric acid is used as the electrolyte, while the electrodes are plates made of lead dioxide (PbO) and spongy lead. These batteries are also called lead accumulators or storage batteries. Batteries used in cars, trucks, and inverters are examples of secondary batteries.

stem: The compound which on dissolution in water makes it hard, is

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above 3 2

expl: Hardness of water is due to the presence of soluble bicarbonates, chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium. Bicarbonates cause temporary hardness, which can be removed by boiling the water, e.g., calcium bicarbonate [Ca(HCO ) ]. Chlorides and sulphates cause permanent hardness, which cannot be removed by boiling. Permanent hardness can be removed only by chemical reactions, e.g., magnesium sulphate (MgSO ), calcium chloride (CaCl), etc. Therefore, option (d) is correct.

stem: Which of the following will have the maximum weight?
expl: Molecular weight of sucrose (C H O ) = 12 × atomic weight of C + 22 × atomic weight + 11 × atomic weight of O = (12×12) + (22×1) + (11×16) = 342 g/mol Weight of 0.2 mole of sucrose = 342 × 0.2 = 68.4 g Weight of CO = (12×1) + (16×2) = 44 g/mol Weight of 2 moles of CO = 44 × 2 = 88 g Weight of 2 moles of CaCO = 2 × [(1× atomic weight of Ca) + (1× atomic weight of C) + (3× atomic weight of O)] = 2 × (40 + 12 + 3×16) = 200 g Therefore, among the given options, the weight of 2 moles of CaCO is the maximum.

stem: Which of the following is not an electrophile?
expl: Na+ is not a true electrophile because it already has a stable outer-shell configuration. Electrophiles may be positively charged or may have vacant orbitals. H+ and BF – are examples of electrophiles.
